memory_candidates.content: When broadening a 'script-invocation identity' matcher used to decide whether an automated sweep may delete an entry, an absolute (/-leading) path with no recognized project-relative anchor (e.g. no '.claude/' substring) must be treated as identity-INELIGIBLE even if it technically contains a *.sh invocation -- otherwise a hand-written/custom entry at an arbitrary absolute path becomes sweep-eligible and can be silently deleted by an empty or unrelated valid-set. This was a required-but-unstated third exclusion beyond the two literally specified in the originating plan.

For a bash test suite that must exercise a 'bridge failure' (a helper binary/script missing or broken) without risking the real file, add a single env-var override at the production script's own resolution site (e.g. HOOK_IDENTITY_CLI_OVERRIDE) defaulting to the real path. This is cheaper and safer than renaming/moving the real file mid-test-run, and keeps the override visible at the exact line the real path is resolved.

A matcher string used as a composite key component (e.g. event+matcher+identity) can itself legitimately contain the chosen field separator (observed: Claude Code hook matchers like 'Bash|Write|Edit' contain literal pipe characters). Use a control character (e.g. '\1') as the join separator for such composite keys, never a character that can appear in real field data.
